correctness.rationale: The length partition is exhaustive. For n of length <=k, alternating reflections force arithmetic-progression one-bit positions and the progression step divides k. Equal-length addition flips a carry interval whose reflection symmetry forces a singleton middle bit at index k. Length overflow is impossible for length >=k+2 because bit 1 must simultaneously be one and zero; length k+1 has a unique form by digit induction. Conversely all three families consist of palindromes separated by 2^k; disjoint lengths yield exact count. No nonstandard lemma is assumed. A standalone standard-library checker enumerated all pairs through the proven length bound for k=2..14, totaling 16,435 pairs; finite checks supplement but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: [1, Question 26] explicitly requests estimates of finite fixed-gap multiplicities. This exact formula and complete classification solve a natural infinite one-parameter subfamily given by single-bit binary differences; they expose three structurally distinct carry regimes and an unexpected additive divisor-function term. The result determines an exact natural invariant and is not a routine consequence of the prior finiteness criterion.
